Answer: D
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates bilateral pleural effusions (blunted costophrenic angles and basal opacities) and associated compressive atelectasis, which mechanically reduce lung volume and explain the acute respiratory distress. While a pacemaker is present, there is no radiographic evidence of valve displacement or primary alveolar edema pattern to support the other options.
